catalog_quote: Crowley 2002:661, sec.1.3 Stress: "Stress falls on the penultimate syllable. A final long vowel or diphthong causes stress to be optionally moved to the final syllable." ... p.660: "Vowel length is contrastive, but the data do not provide any evidence for the existence of a contrastive /o:/. Vowel length has very low functional load in this language in any case." ... p.660 sec.1.2: "Word final consonants are permitted, but otherwise all intramorphemic syllables are open." || Parker 1968:89 (StressTyp2 carried quote): "Monosyllables are stressed. Bisyllabic major words are stressed on the first syllable if the second is short. Otherwise stress is variable or constant through both syllables. In trisyllabic words, the pattern is much the same on the final two syllables."

audit.recode_to: weight-sensitive (not hedged): stress final if the final syllable is heavy (closed CVC or long vowel/diphthong CVV), otherwise penultimate; wcls CVV+CVC; deciding source Ridge 2019:126, with Crowley 2002/Parker 1968 'optional/variable' final stress kept as a caution note (older description, possibly level stress or dialect variation, cf. Ridge p.35 Toak).
audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding Crowley 2002:661 quotation is verbatim in the held djvu text and excerpt; the Parker 1968:89 wording is second-hand via StressTyp2 as the record states. (2) The coding rests on a 2002 sketch adapted from a 1968 article; the record's heavy class is CVV only and it notes 'word-final consonants... not mentioned as attracting stress', and it codes the weight effect as optional (QS-HEDGED). (3) Ridge 2019, a 426-pp fieldwork dissertation we already hold (used only for the morphology lane), gives a categorical rule with closed AND long-vowel finals attracting stress, supported by stress-marked examples and clitic stress-shift diagnostics. That changes two fields (hedge -> categorical; wcls CVV -> CVV+CVC), so the record is at-risk and should be recoded on Ridge 2019:126, keeping Parker/Crowley's optionality as a caution since Ridge's stress analysis is impressionistic (p.401)

sources.quote: 'Main word stress in Vatlongos falls on the final syllable if that syllable has a consonant coda or a long vowel (analysed as bimoraic syllable structures), and the penultimate syllable if the final syllable has a short vowel (analysed as monomoraic syllables)'; enclitics =ti shift stress onto a preceding final short syllable (la.'va.ti, ku.'hi.ti); secondary stress marked in (156)-(158) e.g. li.,naa.va.'si.ti.
